summary.headline: SJS Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.9% YoY to Rs 2,827.3 mn with record 31% EBITDA margin, but FY27 growth guidance was cut to 1.2x-1.5x industry.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.9% YoY to Rs 2,827.3 mn and PAT rose 34.8% to Rs 583.3 mn (20.6% margin), both company records on a quarterly basis. EBITDA margin hit 31% (up 144 bps), helped by product rationalisation, exports and mix, while non-auto (consumer) revenue fell after a low-margin business was exited and a high-margin successor export order was hit by West Asia disruption. Management cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1.2x-1.5x industry (from 1.5x-2x) and raised EBITDA margin guidance to 29-30% (from 27-28%). Capacity additions (Decoplast chrome plating, Bengaluru, Walter Pack consolidation, display plant) are coming online through 2027.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,327.5 mn; includes one-time gain Rs 241.7 mn on sale of old Bangalore facility

financial_highlights.change: Lower QoQ as Walter Pack intangible amortisation runs off (~Rs 10 mn per quarter impact)

segments.name: Passenger vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 43.3% of Q2 revenue; growth led by passenger vehicles. Automotive revenue grew 21.7% YoY vs industry 13.2% for PV plus motorcycles in Q2 (H1: +26.6% vs 15.3%).

segments.name: Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed 38.9% of Q2 revenue. Portfolio weighted to motorcycles; scooters (industry +30.1%) grew faster than motorcycles (+9.8%), where SJS has limited scooter exposure.

segments.name: Consumer and others (incl. Walter Pack)
segments.commentary: Contributed 17.8% of Q2 revenue and was weak: exit of a low-margin large consumer business at WPI, and a high-margin successor export order hit by West Asia conflict and weak North America demand.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q2 exports Rs 282.5 mn, +23.1% YoY, 10% of revenue; H1 exports +45.8%. Target 14-15% of revenue by FY28.

segments.name: SJS Decoplast (chrome plating)
segments.commentary: New Pune chrome plating plant started August 2026 (2x capacity); FY25 revenue about Rs 240 crore, potential about Rs 500 crore on new capacity. Tata Motors added as customer.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth recalibrated to 1.2x-1.5x of PV plus motorcycle industry growth, from 1.5x-2x earlier; management said this applies to the next one to two quarters, with growth expected to recover.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance raised to 29-30% from 27-28%.
Management said absolute rupee EBITDA and PAT for FY27 will be in line with the original plan at the start of the year.
Export contribution target of 14-15% of consolidated revenue by FY28.
Display market expected at Rs 5,000-7,000 crore by 2030-31; internal target of about 10% share (Rs 500-700 crore revenue by 2031).
Depreciation to step up from Q3 FY27 as Pune chrome, Bangalore and other assets are capitalised.
capex_capacity: Total capex plan FY26-FY28 Rs 2,700-2,850 mn; Rs 1,310.6 mn incurred so far (Rs 822 mn in FY26, Rs 488.6 mn in H1 FY27); remaining funded from internal accruals.
Bengaluru expansion complete, about 20% capacity addition (roof built on existing building, about 40,000 sq ft); commercial production likely Q3 FY27.
Walter Pack consolidating three Ranjangaon plants into one facility; expected to commence by May 2027. SJS acquired remaining 9.9% of WPI for Rs 199.22 mn.
SJS Display Electronics Pune display plant capex Rs 65 crore (Rs 25 crore local bonding, Rs 40 crore glass); operational Q2 FY28; expected asset turn about 3.5x (4-5x bonding, 2-3x glass).
Standalone SJS utilisation about 60% after new capacity (70-75% earlier); management sees 80-85% as achievable; no new standalone capacity needed for about two to three years.
demand_pricing: Industry context: India automotive production +17.8% in Q2 FY27; PV +24.9%, two-wheelers +16.5%.
Gross margin 56.5% despite higher raw material, crude and startup costs; management credits mix, exports and exit of low-margin products.

New wins in Q2 from TVS, Mahindra, Hero MotoCorp, Stellantis, Maruti Suzuki, Bajaj Auto, Royal Enfield, Whirlpool, Godrej; new customers HARMAN and TADME (Toyota Middle East); Tata Motors added for chrome plating.
Management flagged pricing pressure across the industry and weaker consumer OEM sentiment amid elevated commodity prices.
Two-wheeler scooter pipeline: management says it is now in discussions to attack the scooter segment using chrome/garnish capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Upside to back-half outlook if crude and metal costs correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects consumer demand to improve with clearer macro and softer input costs; capacity now in place to restart exports and domestic growth, with revenue expected back on trajectory over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company cutting growth guidance despite outperforming the market by about 1.7x?
qa_highlights.answer: Cut attributed to one large export consumer business lost to West Asia disruption and motorcycle focus versus scooters; management said outperformance continues and guidance was set for abundant caution.

qa_highlights.question: Which lower-margin products were pruned and what is driving depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Pruning done in the last two quarters, including a large low-margin consumer business at WPI; depreciation fell on Walter Pack intangible run-off (about Rs 10 mn), and will rise from Q3 as new capacity is capitalised.

qa_highlights.question: Non-auto business weakness and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-auto was hit by exit of a low-margin WPI customer and the West Asia-driven delay of a high-margin consumer export order; management expects recovery in one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Chrome plating revenue potential and display capex and asset turn?
qa_highlights.answer: Chrome plating capacity could reach about Rs 500 crore from about Rs 240 crore in FY25, with next doubling targeted in three to four years; display capex Rs 65 crore with about 3.5x average asset turn.

qa_highlights.question: Display business ramp and 2031 revenue expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Display market expected at Rs 5,000-7,000 crore by 2030-31; internal target of at least 10% share (Rs 500-700 crore by 2031), with other businesses growing 1.5x-2x industry.

risks_watch: Guidance cut to 1.2x-1.5x industry growth; watch whether H2 FY27 revenue growth recovers as management expects within one to two quarters.
Consumer and export recovery depends on West Asia conflict and North America demand; WPI successor export order delayed.
Scooter exposure remains limited while scooter segment outgrows motorcycles; watch scooter wins.
Depreciation step-up from Q3 FY27 and ramp-up costs at Decoplast, Bangalore and Walter Pack consolidation (May 2027) may pressure margins.
Display business (BOE Varitronix partnership) is a new business with unproven ramp; Pune plant due Q2 FY28.
Q2 PAT includes no one-time gain, but H1 reported PAT includes Rs 241.7 mn one-time gain on Bangalore facility sale.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and capacity, but explicitly cautious on near-term growth: management lowered revenue growth guidance and attributed the slowdown to West Asia disruption, consumer weakness and product pruning, while repeatedly stating outperformance and EBITDA commitments are intact.
key_quotes: So, our EBITDA has grown to a record 31.0%, and essentially what we see with commodity prices easing, hopefully, let's hope that crude comes down and all the other commodities come down, that should improve buying sentiment.
We have been circumspect that let us build capacity first before we target new customers.
We see no challenge at all in terms of meeting our commitments, in terms of EBITDA and PAT.
Think of us as a very high - growth, high-profit company.

adds.what: Bengaluru expansion, ~20% capacity addition (roof on existing building, ~40,000 sq ft)
SJS Decoplast new Pune chrome plating plant (2x capacity)
Walter Pack consolidation of three Ranjangaon plants into one facility
SJS Display Electronics Pune display plant (Rs 65 crore capex)

growth.why: FY27 auto revenue growth guidance cut to 1.2x-1.5x PV+motorcycle industry growth (from 1.5x-2x), while EBITDA margin guidance was raised to 29-30%; backing is partial, with Bengaluru, Pune chrome and Walter Pack capacity plus new wins, but consumer weakness and pricing pressure temper outlook.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin guidance raised to 29-30% from 27-28% and Q2 margin hit 31% (+144 bps YoY) on mix, exports and product exits, though depreciation steps up from Q3 and Decoplast/Bengaluru/Walter Pack ramp costs weigh.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New Pune chrome plating plant started Aug 2026 (2x capacity), and Bengaluru ~20% capacity addition has commercial production likely Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided FY27 growth to 1.2x-1.5x PV+motorcycle industry (from 1.5x-2x) and expects recovery in 1-2 quarters; Q2 automotive grew 21.7% vs industry 13.2% and H1 exports +45.8%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Standalone utilisation is about 60% (70-75% earlier) and no new standalone capacity is needed for 2-3 years; FY26-28 capex plan of Rs 2,700-2,850 mn is held and mostly already committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue growth guidance was cut to 1.2x-1.5x industry; only EBITDA margin guidance was raised (27-28% to 29-30%), and rupee EBITDA/PAT stay in line with the original plan.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue guide already cut once; consumer exports hit by West Asia and North America weakness, and management flagged industry pricing pressure and elevated commodity costs.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Display plant (Rs 65 crore capex) operational Q2 FY28, targeting ~10% share of a Rs 5,000-7,000 crore market by 2030-31; scooter chrome/garnish push under discussion.

rows.label: Export share to 14-15% by FY28
rows.why: Exports were 10% of Q2 revenue (Rs 282.5 mn, +23.1% YoY) and H1 exports grew 45.8%, with the target held at 14-15%.

rows.label: Scooter segment entry via chrome/garnish
rows.why: Scooters grew 30.1% industry-wide vs motorcycles 9.8%, and management says it is now in discussions to attack scooters, but no wins are yet disclosed.

rows.label: Decoplast chrome plating revenue scale-up
rows.why: Chrome plating revenue of about Rs 240 crore in FY25 could reach about Rs 500 crore on new capacity, with Tata Motors added as a customer.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, capacity and outperformance, but cautious on near-term growth after cutting FY27 revenue guidance; analysts pressed on why growth was cut despite outperforming the market by about 1.7x.
